formatted_text: **Slow down and look out for pedestrians** who may be crossing the road.[cite: 30]
**Slow down immediately and look out for children** who could be crossing the road unexpectedly or even be playing the road.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and be on the look out for cyclists** using or crossing the road for the next 2 km.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and be on the look out** for the next 2 km **for animals**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and be on the look out** for the next 2 km **for wild animals**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and be prepared to stop** should the gates be closing or are closed.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and make sure there is no oncoming traffic** about to cross the same gate.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and look to the right and left for oncoming trains**.[cite: 30] If a train is approaching **stop in time**, but **not within the railway crossing reserve**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and switch your car's headlights on in the dim position**.[cite: 30]
If your vehicle is higher than the bridge or structure as indicated by this sign, **find an alternative route**.[cite: 30]
**Find an alternative route** if your vehicle is longer that the length indicated in metres on this sign.[cite: 30]

**Be aware of slow-moving traffic**, particularly in mountainous areas with sharp curves.[cite: 30] **Allow for a longer stopping distance** on a descent and especially when your vehicle is heavily laden.[cite: 30]

**Slow down** and, particularly in mountainous areas with sharp curves, **be able to stop within the distance you can see**.[cite: 30] Remember to **allow for a longer stopping distance** on a descent especially when your vehicle is heavily laden.[cite: 30]

**Slow down and look out for a ditches or potholes** at the joint between the gravel and the tarred surface.[cite: 30] Steering will be lighter on the gravel, vehicles will tend to skid easier and will **need a longer stopping distance**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down** and, if there is oncoming traffic, **try not to cross the bridge at the same time** as an approaching vehicle.[cite: 30]
**Slow down** if there is oncoming traffic, **stop at least 6m from the structure and yield to the other vehicle**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and adjust your position** on the carriageway since oncoming vehicles will pass close to you.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and adjust your position** on the roadway.[cite: 30]
**Slow down to avoid potholes** without endangering other traffic.[cite: 30]
**Slow down so that you can drive over the speed humps** without damaging your vehicle or losing control.[cite: 30]
**Slow down** since any sudden braking or harsh steering could cause your vehicle to start skidding sooner than usual for the next 2 km.[cite: 30]

**Slow down to be able to stop within their sight distance** if a fall occurs or has occurred.[cite: 30] Such falls occur more often when it rains and therefore **reduce your speed further** since your stopping distance during rainy weather will be longer.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and look out for other temporary road traffic signs**, people regulating the traffic or who might be crossing the road.[cite: 30]

**Slow down and drive slowly past the grader**.[cite: 30] The full width of the road may not be available and there could be sand or gravel on the carriageway that could affect the handling of their vehicles.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and be aware** that oncoming vehicles could throw up stones that could cause damage.[cite: 30] Your vehicle's braking and turning capacity could also be affected negatively.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and look out for anything** on or next to the carriageway that could cause you to change speed or direction.[cite: 30]

**Slow down and be aware** that your vehicle may tend to the left or right if you straddle the step between the higher and lower level.[cite: 30] Because of the ridge vehicles may also be slow to return to the higher level and could react suddenly if the wheel mounts the ridge.[cite: 30] **Do not make any sudden jerking steering motions**, because it could cause you to lose control completely.[cite: 30]

**Do not drive or stop on the shoulder**.[cite: 30] If this is unavoidable, for example to avoid a collision, **slow down as much as possible** because the vehicle will pull in the direction of the shoulder when you move off the road.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and get ready to stop**.[cite: 30]

**Look out for trucks** that could force you to slow down.[cite: 30] **Slow down and look out for trucks** that want to cross or join the road.[cite: 30] Also **look out for anything spilt or dropped on the road** by the trucks like gravel, sand or water that could affect the handling of your vehicle.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and look out for other road traffic signs** that indicate a specific hazard.[cite: 30]
**Be ready to stop at the stop sign** that follows after the flashing blue light or on demand of a police officer.[cite: 30]
**Slow down and look out for the end of the road** so that you can stop in time.[cite: 30]

**Determine if a wind is blowing and from which direction**.[cite: 30] Any shielding of the wind by a truck, bridge or excavation will affect your vehicle and you should **adjust the steering in time**.[cite: 30]
**Slow down** and if it is not known how deep the water is, **stop**.[cite: 30] If passable, **drive through the water slowly**.[cite: 30]
**Do not get a frightened and do not brake suddenly**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for agricultural vehicles and slow down** of they want to cross the road or are crossing it.[cite: 30]

**Slow down immediately, look out for someone controlling the traffic and be ready to stop**.[cite: 30] If there is enough or professional help on the scene, **do not stop out of curiosity**.[cite: 30] **Do not look at the collision scene or wreckage**, concentrate on the route to be followed without driving over or into anything.[cite: 30]
**Look out for Fog or smoke and slow down**.[cite: 30] **Be on the look out for other slow moving vehicles**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for slow moving vehicle and adapt speed accordingly**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for horses and riders ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for elephants ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for warthogs ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop**.[cite: 30]
**Look out for hippos ahead and be prepared to slow down or stop**.[cite: 30]
**Do not continue** of your vehicle is wider than indicated on the sign.[cite: 30]
**Look out for electrical cables** on the road way ahead.[cite: 30]
**Look out for an asphalt, tar or concrete road ahead**.[cite: 30]
**Do not pass to the right** of W401 or TW401 **and to the left** of W402 or TW402.[cite: 30]
**Slow down** to take the curve at a safe speed or to be able to stop within the distance you can see.[cite: 30]
**Slow down to turn left or right or to stop**.[cite: 30]
